title: Why Curation Bots Were Made: Whale Coverage and Minnow Aggregation
provenanceNote: Hand-authored educational seed for knowledge/steem-economy/. Article 2 of 3 — the HISTORY, told honestly. Two origin stories: (1) whale content-coverage (whales can't manually read 8,000+ posts/day -> auto-voters, curation trails, delegation to guilds; canonical @steemed/@itsascam example) and (2) minnow aggregation (a small vote is worth ~0 / below dust -> guilds, delegation pools, bid bots). Frames both as the same delegation+automation primitive pointed opposite ways. Honest abuse section: vote-selling/bid bots (Sybil-value critique), self-voting, circle-jerks, passive bid-bot delegation, bot saturation/tone-deafness. Then Steem's HF21/EIP fix (50/50 split, convergent-linear curve, FREE DOWNVOTE POOL) and the KEY point that MELEK is a no-downvote Blurt-style fork so it CANNOT use downvote cleanup and instead uses quality-gating/curation-weighting/no-paid-votes/transparency. Sources: family steem_bots_history.json for coverage+saturation; SteemitBlog + Tim Cliff for EIP; SteemAuto for trails. HARD compliance: neutral, not-investment-advice, abuses attributed to the cited community's framing. Written 2026-08-27 (memory: whale-dolphin-minnow-education-infrastructure).
